::: {.solutions}

**Show all your reasoning.** Total: **37 marks** · Suggested time: **50 minutes**.

Two rules do most of the work:

> **Outside the bracket → changes $y$, does as it says. Inside the bracket → changes $x$, does the
> opposite** (and $f(ax)$ stretches by $\tfrac1a$).

> **An expression built from $f(x)$:** let $w=f(x)$, read the range of $w$, finish it as an ordinary
> max/min in $w$ — **turning points *and* endpoints.**

| Section | What it covers | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Fluency** | single transformations; images of points | 11 |
| **B — Exam standard** | modulus graphs; function-of-a-function | 17 |
| **C — Stretch** | combined transformations; counting solutions | 9 |

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Answer form.** Turning points → **coordinates** $(x,y)$. "How many solutions" → **a whole number**.
Sketches → label every root, turning point, and axis intercept.
:::

# Section A — Fluency

## Question 1 **[4]**

The graph of $y=f(x)$ has its maximum at $(3,5)$. State the coordinates of the maximum of each of the
following.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) $\;y=f(x)-2$ **[1]** &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; (b) $\;y=f(x+4)$ **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) $\;y=4f(x)$ **[1]** &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; (d) $\;y=f\!\left(\tfrac{x}{2}\right)$ **[1]**

# Section B — Exam standard

## Question 4 **[6]**

Let $f(x)=(x-3)(x+1)$ — a parabola with roots $x=-1$ and $x=3$ and minimum at $(1,-4)$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Sketch $\;y=\lvert f(x)\rvert$, labelling the roots and the turning point. **[2]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) Sketch $\;y=f(\lvert x\rvert)$, labelling the roots and the turning points. **[2]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) How many solutions does $\;\lvert f(x)\rvert = 2\;$ have? Justify. **[2]**

The graph of $y=f(x)$ has range $1\le f(x)\le5$. Find the **maximum** and **minimum** values of
$$\bigl(f(x)\bigr)^2 - 6f(x) + 10,$$
and hence the difference between them.

## Question 8 **[4]**

The graph of $y=f(x)$ has a single maximum value of $4$, reached at $x=0$; $f(x)>0$ for all $x$, and
$f(x)\to0$ as $x\to\pm\infty$ (a single symmetric "bump").

How many solutions does $\;\bigl(f(x)\bigr)^2 - 5f(x) + 4 = 0\;$ have? Justify.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Before you hand this in

For every "function-of-a-function" question (5, 6, 8): did you **substitute $w=f(x)$ first**, and did you
check **both the turning point *and* the endpoints** of the range? Missing an endpoint is the commonest
way these go wrong.
:::
